1.explanation:
1) Table.js is the root of the React DataTable — it renders the `<table>` element but does not forward a passed-in `style` prop (and so any `--row-height` variable) to the real DOM node.
2) TableRow.js renders each `<tr>` in the body; it takes props from `getRowProps` but does not apply a passed `style.height` or CSS var to the row.
3) TableHeader.js renders the header `<tr>` and `<th>` cells; like TableRow, it does not forward a `style` prop or apply a CSS custom property for row height.
4) DataTable/DataTable.mdx is the documentation for the React DataTable — it needs to be updated to document the new “medium” row-height option and show how to consume `--row-height` when styling the table.
1.bug_scenario: The goal is to give Carbon’s React DataTable a third “medium” (40 px) row-height variant (in addition to the existing “compact” and “short” modes) and/or allow consumers to override row height via the CSS custom property `--row-height`. In the repro we pass `<Table style={{ '--row-height': '40px' }}>` and even set `<TableRow style={{ height: '40px' }}>`, but neither the header nor the body rows pick up this new height. In other words, neither the DataTable wrapper nor its row/header components forward the custom CSS variable or inline height to the DOM, so the table stays at the default row height.

2.explanation:
All of the core rendering logic for row height lives in the React DataTable implementation. 

• Table.js – this file defines the <Table> component’s size prop, its allowed values, and the mapping from size ("compact", "short" etc.) to the matching CSS class or CSS variable. We need to add “md” to its propTypes/defaultProps and implement the 40px mapping.

• DataTable.js – the top‐level wrapper that reads incoming props and passes size (and default size) down to Table. It needs to accept and pass through the new “md” option.

• TableRow.js – this file is responsible for rendering each <tr> and applies inline styles or classNames based on table size. It needs to recognize the new 40px variant so that rows render at the requested height.

• TableHeader.js – similar to TableRow.js but for the header <th> row. It also applies style or className for the header height and must be updated for the 40px size.

Updating these four files will allow consumers to use size="md" (or an equivalent new prop) and have the table render with 40px row and header heights consistently, without manually overriding CSS variables or inline styles.
2.bug_scenario: The Carbon React DataTable currently only ships with the default, “short” (32px), and “compact” (24px) heights. The request is to add a new “md” (40px) row‐height option so that table rows and headers can render at 40px high. In the reproduction the user resorts to inline styles ("--row-height: 40px" on the <Table> and style={{ height: '40px' }} on each <TableRow>), because the component’s built‐in size variants do not include a 40px option. We need to extend the React DataTable code so that a “md” size prop (or similar) maps to 40px and surfaces via the correct CSS class or CSS variable, just like the other sizes.
